claims: n109_kaggle/n109_tomkodaj.yaml states 109 unit squares as a packing.squares:Witness/v2 document of rational corners at side 547464479047171949843/50000000000000000000 = 10.94928958094343899686, rounded up s(109) <= 10.949289580944; its squares are numbered square-0 to square-108. The README and the comment say it is an exact transcription of the 109 rows of n109_tomkodaj.csv, each orientation by a rational tan(angle/2) so every square has exactly unit sides, and the centres translated into the first quadrant. The comment says the issue's 10.949289580943 was rounded to nearest.

n109_kaggle/n109_tomkodaj.csv holds, by the README and the comment, the original header and the 109 rows for n = 109 of Tomáš Kodaj's Kaggle dataset 'Squares in Squares: strips and bands (coordinates)', version 2, 13 November 2026, CC0, unchanged (centres, angle in radians); his notebook squares-in-squares-22-1636 copies the same submission.csv to its output, whose full SHA-256 they give as 7700b20d7c901a831741d0dbabae0941fefe460381cc18d969ec29aa728e489b (not checkable here).

verification.txt says this repository's independent rational-corner checker at jlevy/squares f9ddfeeef9070ede581142154ab992149b278ab0 reports 'VERIFIED: 109 squares, 5886 pairs' with the exact side and a least pair gap of 3200000000000000400000000000001/1600000000000000000000000000000400000000000000 (about 2.0e-15).

On credit the README and the comment say that Kodaj publishes the coordinates and refers to his source notebooks for the original credits; that Navneet Prabhat's public compilation contains the same packing (side about 10.94928958094337); that Guilherme Dias da Fonseca published the 109-square pinwheel earlier (6 November 2026, side 10.949392392); that #958 documents a public pinwheel in Samanyu-dev's best_fit_101_500.csv at 10.94928958094538; and that who made the last numerical refinement is unconfirmed. The comment asks that it be credited as this repository's sources support. The README says the transcription was made with GPT-6.2 Sol (OpenAI) and checked again with Claude (Anthropic), under the direction of Joost de Winter, and that the packing is not his work.
